blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight to the Galápagos Islands. On arrival at Baltra Airport, your guide will meet you and help with your luggage.

It takes about 10 minutes to reach the Itabaca Channel, followed by a motorboat crossing of about five minutes to Santa Cruz Island. From there, Puerto Ayora is about a 45-minute drive. Along the way, the island's dry, reddish north gradually gives way to greener highlands.

The group will stop in the Santa Cruz highlands, where farmland borders areas of natural habitat. The birds here include the famous Galápagos finches associated with Charles Darwin's research.

The main focus of the visit is seeing giant land tortoises in their natural habitat. On private farms, you can see tortoises of different ages and sizes. Young tortoises generally have smooth, glossy shells, while older ones show the marks of a long life. Your guide will explain how local farms help protect these animals and the areas where they feed and roam.

You will also stop at the lava tunnels. They formed as lava flows cooled, with the outer layer hardening faster than the interior. Some tunnels have collapsed, but sections remain that can be explored on foot. Inside, there are narrow passages and fallen blocks of rock. The visit offers a look at the tunnels' structure and how they formed.

Lunch is included. After the tour, transfer to Puerto Ayora, check in to your hotel and enjoy free time. You can walk around town, explore the waterfront or browse the souvenir shops.

**Accommodation:** Solymar 4*, Ocean View Room.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch.
Frigatebird with an inflated red throat pouch perched on a branch on North Seymour Island, Galápagos, Ecuador
North Seymour Island: a black frigatebird with a bright red throat pouch

Early in the morning, you will leave your hotel for the Itabaca Channel, where you will board a yacht. The crossing takes about two hours. You can watch the ocean along the way, and in favourable conditions dolphins and other marine animals may appear near the yacht.

After landing on Bartolomé, you will hike uphill for about 30 minutes. The trail crosses a volcanic landscape that in places looks like the surface of another planet. The summit offers views of Santiago, North Seymour, Baltra, Santa Cruz, Rábida and the small island of Chinese Hat. You can also see Pinnacle Rock, a remnant of an ancient eroded volcano and one of the most recognisable silhouettes in the Galápagos.

After the walk, the excursion continues along the coast. From the boat, you may see Galápagos penguins, about 50 cm tall, standing by the rocks or darting through the clear water.

Next comes time at the beach and for snorkelling. Galápagos penguins, reef sharks, sea stars, rays, sea turtles and colourful tropical fish can be found in the shallows. Along the shore, you may see marine iguanas, sea lions and pelicans.

After the day's activities, lunch is served on board. The yacht returns by evening, leaving time for a walk around Puerto Ayora.

**Accommodation:** Solymar 4*, Ocean View Room.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch.
